turns.ctx: The M5Stack Cardputer v1.1 (SKU K132-V11) is a card-sized computer for engineers and makers. turns.ctx: NEC is a common infrared remote protocol: each button sends an 8-bit address (the device) and an 8-bit command (the button) on a 38 kHz carrier. Card sends NEC with: send ir address 4 command 8. To find codes, read the original remote with an IR receiver, or look up the device's NEC code list.

turns.ctx: The Grove port supplies 5V on the red wire, but the G1 and G2 signals are 3.3 V logic. Do not drive G1 or G2 with 5V signals. Analog sensors on G1 or G2 can be read with analogRead(); the ADC reads 0 to about 3.1 V.
turns.user: can I hook up a 5v sensor to g1 or g2?
turns.bot: The G1 and G2 signals are 3.3 V logic. Do not drive G1 or G2 with 5V signals, or you may damage the ESP32-S3.

turns.ctx: The Cardputer v1.1 has no IMU (no accelerometer or gyroscope), no humidity or room temperature sensor, no light sensor, no GPS, no camera and no vibration motor. turns.ctx: Cardputer v1.1 vs the original Cardputer: v1.1 uses the Stamp-S3A instead of the StampS3, has an optimised antenna, a bigger boot key, lower power use, and an RGB LED that shares power with the screen backlight (the original powered the LED as soon as it was switched on).

turns.ctx: NEC is a common infrared remote protocol: each button sends an 8-bit address (the device) and an 8-bit command (the button) on a 38 kHz carrier. turns.bot: NEC protocol uses 8 bits for both address and command, which limits each value to a maximum of 255.
